Parallel cell metadata reports actual parallel use, five subagents, completed evaluation, artifact copy success, and official failure at 36 of 70 cases.
Parallel status confirms swarm mode, one completed agent attempt, five subagents, artifact files under test7.mjs plus hash, pbkdf2, and cli directories, and current official evaluation failure.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event journal records session creation, prompt, tool calls, five subagent completions, final verification commands, and prompt completion.
Session index maps the parallel Kimi session id to the workspace session directory and /workspace working directory.
Agent 0 received the SHA-1 module brief, wrote /output/hash/sha1.mjs, ran known vector and boundary checks, and returned a completed SHA-1 summary.
Agent 1 received the HMAC module brief, wrote /output/hash/hmac.mjs, syntax checked it, ran RFC-style HMAC checks once SHA-1 existed, and returned completion.
Agent 2 received the PBKDF2 module brief, wrote /output/pbkdf2/pbkdf2.mjs, fixed its read-buffer logic, verified PBKDF2 behavior in a temporary harness, and returned completion.
Agent 3 received the CLI parser brief, wrote /output/cli/args.mjs, exercised normal and error parsing cases, removed its temporary test file, and returned completion.
Agent 4 received the entry-point brief, wrote /output/test7.mjs, syntax checked it while sibling modules were still absent, and returned completion for its file.

Parallel parent entered swarm mode, probed PBKDF2 behavior, dispatched five compatible file-scoped children, collected the aggregate swarm result, ran integrated sample and edge checks, and ended with a completion summary.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is the same pbkdf2/test7.py migration request with ESM .mjs output, manual CLI parsing, no external dependencies, black-box probing, and /output delivery.

Serial evaluation summary records a completed official RepoZero Py2JS evaluation with 36 passed samples out of 70 and solution_passed false.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the core requirements: implement PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 with 1000 iterations and UTF-8 strings, use ESM .mjs files, split functionality into modules, manually parse --a/--b/--c, and avoid external dependencies.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: After a short executable probe, the parent used one AgentSwarm call with five distinct owners: SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, CLI parsing, and the test7.mjs entry point. The parent retained final verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the agreed hierarchical files under /output/hash, /output/pbkdf2, /output/cli, and /output/test7.mjs. PBKDF2 child corrected its streaming read logic before reporting completion.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent collected all five child summaries from the aggregate swarm result and then exercised the final assembled /output/test7.mjs against the executable before final response. Status shows the hierarchical artifact was copied.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification included visible sample cases, some edge cases, and component-level child checks. It did not reveal the hidden official failures, and official evaluation later passed only 36 of 70.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: At closure the visible tests passed, but the current official evaluator marks the submitted solution failed at 36/70. The mounted evidence does not expose the exact hidden-case defect.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 default, 1000 iterations, UTF-8 handling, pure JS ESM output, manual CLI parser, and sample/edge output-matching requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Serial kept all implementation and verification ownership in the main actor, writing SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, CLI, and entry-point files directly without delegation.
serial.implementation: Serial produced a flat set of modules in /output: sha1.mjs, hmac.mjs, pbkdf2.mjs, cli.mjs, and test7.mjs. The entry point encoded strings to UTF-8 byte arrays before calling its PBKDF2 helper.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor wrote all files, integration was direct through local imports. The final status shows the flat artifact set was copied with test7.mjs as the entry file.
serial.verification: Serial ran the visible sample cases plus UTF-8, empty-string, inline flag, and missing-argument checks against the executable. Official evaluation later also passed only 36 of 70.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: At closure the serial visible checks passed, but the current official evaluator marks the submitted solution failed at 36/70. The mounted evidence does not expose the exact hidden-case defect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured the ESM, .mjs, local import, manual CLI, zero dependency, black-box behavior, and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 requirements in the parent swarm prompt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial captured the same prompt requirements and directly reasoned that the Python pbkdf2 default was SHA-1 with 1000 iterations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference is visible; both accepted the same visible target and both ultimately failed official hidden cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into five file-scoped child owners and kept parent-level assembly verification after the aggregate child return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all code generation and verification in the main actor and wrote all module files directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split ownership across compatible modules, while serial used a single-owner implementation path; this did not create a distinct official outcome difference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included explicit import paths, export names, argument parser contract, PBKDF2 streaming contract, and entry-point wiring, and child returns matched those contracts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had all interface decisions locally and used flat imports among its own files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The interface shape differed hierarchically versus flat, but no unresolved cross-agent contract conflict or lossy handoff is visible in the parallel run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children implemented SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, CLI parsing, and the entry point in separate directories, with the PBKDF2 child fixing an identified read-buffer bug.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, CLI parsing, and the entry point as flat files in one write phase.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations used different file layouts and helper APIs, but both delivered a test7.mjs artifact and both scored 36/70 officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All five child agents completed and their summaries returned in the AgentSwarm aggregate before the parent ran end-to-end checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all results were local writes and local verification in the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child result lifecycle but no missing join, trapped result, cancellation, or late promotion is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote to a shared /output tree but to distinct agreed files and directories, and the parent ran the final entry point after the child aggregate returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files in one flat /output tree and imported local flat modules from test7.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had concurrent shared-workspace writes, but there is no same-file collision, overwrite, incompatible interface, or unstable provenance consequence in the evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed child component checks and parent integrated comparisons on the visible sample cases plus edge cases, then declared the migration complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed visible sample comparisons and edge cases against the executable, then declared completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on limited visible checks that missed official hidden failures; this is an ordinary verification-coverage limitation shared by both, not a uniquely parallel coordination failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed within the cell budget in about 240 agent seconds, with five children and no timeout, then closed after parent-level checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed within the cell budget in about 158 agent seconds, with no timeout, then closed after local checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more tokens and wall time because of the swarm, but there is no evidence that budget exhaustion displaced an unfinished required stage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official completed status records both solutions as failed with the same score, 36 passed out of 70. The parallel run used a five-child module split and integrated the returned files before sample and edge checks; the serial run wrote a flat module set directly and ran similar sample and edge checks. The observed task-solving difference is therefore organizational rather than an official pass/fail difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel decomposition produced a hierarchical module layout and completed child returns before parent verification.
Parallel verification showed visible samples and edge cases passing, but this was not sufficient for the official hidden set.
serial_contributors: Serial implemented all modules directly in one main trajectory with a flat layout.
Serial verification also showed visible samples and edge cases passing, but this was not sufficient for the official hidden set.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two attempts used different file organization and helper interfaces.
Both likely share an ordinary implementation or coverage defect exposed by hidden tests, but the mounted evidence does not include the hidden failing cases or artifact contents needed to isolate it.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported strategy comparison only

The parent explicitly retained the integration role by collecting child results and running the final assembled test7.mjs after the swarm completed.
The entry-point child owned test7.mjs and the parent verified the final artifact; there was no unowned final placement or package step.
The parallel parent owned the end-to-end transition from probing through child execution, aggregation, integrated checks, and final response.
The parent did a short behavior probe before delegation, but implementation was not blocked behind a long mandatory preflight that caused idle capacity or unfinished work.
There was no separate multi-agent investigation phase followed by deadline-constrained implementation; the swarm directly implemented the component files.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; each required module had an owner and the parent completed integrated checks before closure.
The five-child fan-out completed without timeout and did not consume the budget before required integration or verification could occur.
No single child received an overbroad task that remained unfinished; each child had one bounded module or entry-point responsibility.
The child prompts included the known ESM, .mjs, local import, no dependency, PBKDF2, and delivery contracts, and the returned work followed those contracts.
The parent provided explicit import/export names and paths for every separately owned module, and no incompatible returned interface is visible.
No known finding or current-file fact disappears across a transfer; the parent received all child summaries before running final checks.
The aggregate child report was long but directly usable; the parent proceeded to integrated verification rather than leaving a dependent action unfinished.
No child or parent consumed a superseded workspace state; sibling modules were integrated after all returned and then tested together.
Child returns did not present incompatible contracts requiring adjudication; the agreed imports and exports remained consistent.
The parent made a completion decision after integrated executable comparisons; hidden official failure alone does not prove a parent-visible unresolved integration gap.
The parallel run did not launch a replacement or retry child that repeated prior work without inherited findings.

Completed child summaries were available and the parent used them as the basis for integrated verification and final reporting.
The parent did not wait into a timeout while ignoring available progress; the run completed normally and then verified assembled output.
Parallel children wrote distinct contracted files whose behavior was meant to compose; no competing overlapping design paths required reconciliation.

No non-entry library or module source owned by one agent was replaced by another actor.

There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion step that replaced multiple current outputs and invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Multiple children wrote the shared /output tree, but their file ownership was separated and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem is visible.
No generated temporary file, fixture, cache, tool, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as a stable reference environment.
